ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi rejects the codices' Madinan classification: in his view, the sūra is wholly Makkan, with no Madinan verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Some codices regard it to be Madī nan, which I fail to understand. Not one of its verse is Mad īnan in my opinion

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Calling on anyone besides God resembles chasing a mirage; self-appointed deities and intercessors cannot benefit anyone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Invoking someone other than God is like regarding a mirage to be water and then running after it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Every object in the universe witnesses to God's oneness, and even people's shadows prostrate to Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Every object of this universe, through its very existence, bears witness to the oneness of God. People whose necks do not bend before God

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r17.claim: Ẓill is the visible outline or shadow of an object in light, and similarly in illumination.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r17.anchor: ظل الشيء: ما يظهر من خياله في النور، وبمثله في الضوء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r1.claim: Shadow is originally a verbal noun, then the visible outline of a body; its length and shortening follow the sun’s descent and height.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r1.anchor: الظل مصدر يعني في الأصل، ثم أطلق على الخيال الذي يظهر للجرم، وطوله بسبب انحطاط الشمس، وقصره بسبب ارتفاعها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r2.claim: The shadow is subject to God in its length, shortening, and movement from side to side.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r2.anchor: فهو منقاد لله تعالى في طوله وقصره وميله من جانب إلى جانب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r3.claim: Morning and evening are singled out because shadows grow greatest and most plentiful then; Abū Ḥayyān refers back to his discussion in al-Aʿrāf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r3.anchor: وخص هذان الوقتان بالذكر لأن الظلال إنما تعظم وتكثر فيهما، وتقدم شرح الغدو والآصال في آخر الأعراف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r4.speaker: رُوي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r4.claim: A report says that when a disbeliever prostrates to his idol, his shadow is prostrating to God at that moment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r4.anchor: روي أن الكافر إذا سجد لصنمه كان ظله يسجد لله حينئذ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r5.speaker: أبو مجلز
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r5.claim: Abū Mujliz reads والإيصال in place of الآصال.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز: والإيصال. قال ابن جني: هو مصدر أصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r6.speaker: ابن جني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r6.claim: He parses الإيصال as a verbal noun from aṣala, meaning to enter the late afternoon, like aṣbaḥa means to enter morning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p369/r6.anchor: قال ابن جني: هو مصدر أصل أي: دخل في الأصيل كما تقول: أصبح أي دخل في الإصباح.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.claim: Al-Raʿd’s aim is to portray revelation as true in itself: sometimes its sound and fame move people toward guidance, while sometimes it instead leaves them blind and astray, like thunder whose lightning and rain may benefit, fail, or harm according to where they fall.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.anchor: مقصودها وصف الكتاب بأنه الحق في نفسه ، وتارة يتأثر عنه مع أن له صوتا وصيتا وإرعابا وإرهابا

STUDYQURAN:13:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:13:intro/r7.claim: It highlights natural wonders dependent on God for sustenance; like thunder, they also glorify God.
STUDYQURAN:13:intro/r7.anchor: all of which are entirely dependent upon God for their subsistence

TABATABAI:13:7-16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:7-16/r1.claim: The Qur'an attributes prostration and related acts such as obedience, glorification, praise, and petition to all created things.
TABATABAI:13:7-16/r1.anchor: وهذه النظرة هي التي يعتبرها القرآن الكريم في نسبة السجود وما يناظره من القنوت والتسبيح والحمد والسؤال ونحو ذلك إلى الأشياء

TABATABAI:13:7-16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:7-16/r2.claim: Cosmic prostration is real submission, while bodily prostration in human society has a conventional social meaning and can fail to occur.
TABATABAI:13:7-16/r2.anchor: الغايات موجودة في القسم الأول بحقيقة معناها بخلاف القسم الثاني فإنها إنما توجد فيها بنوع من الوضع والاعتبار

TABATABAI:13:7-16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:7-16/r3.claim: The verse names rational beings to confront the polytheists and urge them to prostrate as other rational beings do; the mention of shadows intensifies the appeal.
TABATABAI:13:7-16/r3.anchor: لأن الكلام في السورة مع المشركين والاحتجاج عليهم فكان في ذلك بعثا لهم أن يسجدوا لله طوعا

TABATABAI:13:7-16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:7-16/r4.claim: All beings are intrinsically and continually submissive to God, so their cosmic prostration is voluntary because none possesses an independent self.
TABATABAI:13:7-16/r4.anchor: ثم إن هذا التذلل والتواضع، الذي هو من عامة الموجودات لساحة ربهم عز وعلا، خضوع ذاتي لا ينفك عنها ولا يتخلف فهو بالطوع البتة

TABATABAI:13:7-16/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:7-16/r5.claim: Material beings may be thwarted by competing causes; they submit unwillingly in what opposes their nature, such as death and decay, and willingly in life, persistence, and reaching perfection.
TABATABAI:13:7-16/r5.anchor: فهذه الأشياء ساجدة لله خاضعة لأمره في جميع الشؤون الراجعة إليها غير أنها فيما يخالف طباعها كالموت والفساد

TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan is credited with taking prostration literally as falling to the ground: believers do so willingly and unbelievers from fear of the sword.
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r1.anchor: وقد نسب القول به إلى الحسن.

TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r2.speaker: الجبائي
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r2.claim: Al-Jubba'i is credited with interpreting prostration as submission: believers submit willingly, while unbelievers submit unwillingly because of pain and illness.

TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r3.claim: Another view says all rational and nonrational beings submit, using a rational form of expression by grammatical predominance.
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r3.anchor: إن المراد بالآية خضوع جميع ما في السماوات والأرض من أولي العقل وغيرهم والتعبير بلفظ يخص أولي العقل للتغليب

TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r4.claim: Al-Tabatabai rejects these interpretations in light of his prior account of cosmic prostration.
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r4.anchor: ومما تقدم يظهر فساد قول بعضهم إن المراد بالسجدة هو الحقيقي منها

TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r5.claim: Although a shadow is privative, its changing length and other effects give it a kind of existence that submits to God in both being and effects.
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r5.anchor: فله نحو من الوجود ذو آثاره يخضع في وجوده وآثاره لله ويسجد له

TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r6.claim: Shadows prostrate voluntarily at all times; dawn and afternoon are singled out because their changing length visibly resembles falling in prostration, unlike their often diminished or absent midday form.
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r6.anchor: وإنما خص بالغدو والآصال بالذكر لا لما قيل إن المراد بهما الدوام

TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r7.claim: The shadow's visible fall is part of what the verse means by prostration, alongside its continual created obedience to God.
TABATABAI:13:7-16#2/r7.anchor: وليس النظر مقصورا على مجرد طاعتها التكوينية في جميع أحوالها وآثارها

TABATABAI:13:7-16#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:7-16#3/r1.claim: The Qur'an's emphasis on shadows is plain in the related verse; this is not poetic fiction but a sensible manifestation that can teach simple minds about rational truths.
TABATABAI:13:7-16#3/r1.anchor: فإن العناية بذلك ظاهرة فيه. وليس ذلك قولا شعريا وتصويرا تخييليا يتوسل به في الدعوة الحقة في كلامه تعالى - وحاشاه -

TABATABAI:13:7-16#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:7-16#3/r2.claim: When truths beyond imagination have a perceptible manifestation, the Qur'an uses it to lead people from sense and imagination toward sound reason; sensory experience can be true and supported by reality.
TABATABAI:13:7-16#3/r2.anchor: كان من الحري أن يستمد به في تعليم الأفهام الساذجة والعقول البسيطة ونقلها من مرتبة الحس والخيال إلى مرحلة العقل السليم

TABATABAI:13:7-16#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16#7/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:13:7-16#7/r2.claim: A report from Abu Ja'far says angels and Muslims born into Islam prostrate willingly, people forced into Islam do so unwillingly, and where people do not prostrate their shadows do so at dawn and afternoon.
TABATABAI:13:7-16#7/r2.anchor: أما من يسجد من أهل السماوات طوعا فالملائكة يسجدون لله طوعا، وأما من يسجد من أهل الأرض ممن ولد في الإسلام فهو يسجد له طوعا،

TABATABAI:13:7-16#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:7-16#7/r3.claim: Al-Tabatabai says the report conflicts with the verse's context: all beings themselves, along with their shadows, are subdued and prostrate in the real cosmic sense, not merely by bodily gestures or shadow resemblance.
TABATABAI:13:7-16#7/r3.anchor: فإن الآية مسوقة لبيان عموم قهره تعالى بعظمته وعلوه من في السماوات والأرض أنفسهم وأظلالهم وهى تنبئ عن سجودها له تعالى بحقيقة السجدة

TABATABAI:13:7-16#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:13:7-16#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:13:7-16#7/r4.claim: He adds that restricting prostration to bodily gestures or shadows resembling prostration fails to glorify God and contradicts the generic reference to shadows in this verse and the broader related passage.
TABATABAI:13:7-16#7/r4.anchor: على أنه لا يوافق العموم المتراءى من قوله { وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال } وأوضح منه العموم الذي في قوله

STUDYQURAN:13:15/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r1.claim: The prostration motif is also found in the cited passages.
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r1.anchor: Cf. 16:48–49; 22:18. Prostrates here expresses the idea of submission, lowliness

STUDYQURAN:13:15/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r2.claim: R explains prostration as submission, lowliness, and inability to refuse; 19:93 describes every creature as a servant.
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r2.anchor: submission, lowliness, and the inability to refuse (R), which is why 19:93 says, There is none in the heavens and on the earth

STUDYQURAN:13:15/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r3.claim: All things are existentially submitted to God at every moment: some recognize this willingly, while others submit unwittingly.
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r3.anchor: all things at all moments are “prostrate,” that is, submitted existentially before God: either they understand this state of affairs and prostrate voluntarily in recognition of it, or they prostrate involuntarily and unwittingly

STUDYQURAN:13:15/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r4.speaker: al-Maybudī
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r4.claim: Al-Maybudī says willing prostration submits to God without hope of reward, while unwilling prostration seeks a benefit or escape from harm.
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r4.anchor: al-Maybudī says that a prostration is done willingly when one submits to God’s Command and Majesty without any hope of reward or gain; the prostration done unwillingly occurs

STUDYQURAN:13:15/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r5.speaker: M
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r5.claim: M says that shadows also submit to God, showing that every aspect of beings is under His sway.
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r5.anchor: As do their shadows is a way of saying that even their shadows submit to God (M), which means that every aspect of their being is under His Sway

STUDYQURAN:13:15/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r6.speaker: N
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r6.claim: N takes morning and evening to imply that creation submits perpetually.
STUDYQURAN:13:15/r6.anchor: and in the morning and the evening implies that they do so perpetually (N). See also 16:48

TAB-FULL:v13p491/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p491/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p491/r1.claim: Despite the pagans' refusal to worship God alone, angels and earthly believers prostrate willingly, while unbelievers do so unwillingly when compelled.
TAB-FULL:v13p491/r1.anchor: ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها

TAB-FULL:v13p491/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p491/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p491/r2.claim: Qatada says believers prostrate willingly, whereas unbelievers prostrate unwillingly.
TAB-FULL:v13p491/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: {ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها}

TAB-FULL:v13p491/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p491/r3.speaker: ربيع بن خثيم
TAB-FULL:v13p491/r3.claim: When reciting the verse, Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym responds, “Indeed, my Lord,” affirming it reverently.
TAB-FULL:v13p491/r3.anchor: إذا تلا هذه الآية: {ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها} قال: «بلى يا رباه»

TAB-FULL:v13p491/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p491/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v13p491/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd explains willing submission as entering Islam voluntarily and unwilling submission as entering only under the sword.
TAB-FULL:v13p491/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها}

TAB-FULL:v13p492/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p492/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p492/r1.claim: The shadows of all who prostrate to God also prostrate morning and evening, as each person's shadow shifts in the evening; compare 16:48.
TAB-FULL:v13p492/r1.anchor: ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال

TAB-FULL:v13p492/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p492/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p492/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the phrase as the time when someone's shadow falls to his right or left.
TAB-FULL:v13p492/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال} [الرعد: 15]

TAB-FULL:v13p492/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p492/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p492/r3.claim: In the interpretation of Mujahid, a believer's shadow prostrates willingly while a disbeliever's shadow does so willingly although he himself is reluctant.
TAB-FULL:v13p492/r3.anchor: قال في تفسير مجاهد: {ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم

TAB-FULL:v13p492/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p492/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v13p492/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says the shadows of all things prostrate to God, citing the shadows that prostrate while humbled.
TAB-FULL:v13p492/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال} [الرعد: 15]

TAB-FULL:v13p492/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p492/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p492/r5.claim: Al-āṣāl is the plural of aṣl, itself the plural of aṣīl, meaning evening from afternoon until sunset; Abu Dhuʾayb's verse uses al-aṣāʾil in this sense.
TAB-FULL:v13p492/r5.anchor: والآصال: جمع أصل، والأصل: جمع أصيل، والأصيل: هو العشي، وهو ما بين العصر إلى مغرب الشمس

TABRISI:13:12-15/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:12-15/r2.speaker: أبو مجلز
TABRISI:13:12-15/r2.claim: Abū Mujliz reads بالغدو والإيصال in a noncanonical reading.

TABRISI:13:12-15/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:12-15/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:12-15/r7.claim: Īṣāl is the verbal noun of āṣalnā, entering or reaching the time of late afternoon.
TABRISI:13:12-15/r7.anchor: والإيصال مصدر آصلنا أي دخلنا في وقت الأصيل

TABRISI:13:12-15/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:12-15/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:12-15/r16.claim: Ẓilāl is the plural of ẓill, the covering cast by a person; ẓill ẓalīl is enduring shade, unlike fayʾ, which returns after sunlight has gone.
TABRISI:13:12-15/r16.anchor: والظلال جمع الظل وهو ستر الشخص ما بإزائه والظل الظليل

TABRISI:13:12-15/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:12-15/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:12-15/r17.claim: Āṣāl is a plural of aṣl, itself a plural of aṣīl; the term evokes the origin of night and denotes the time from ʿaṣr to sunset.
TABRISI:13:12-15/r17.anchor: والآصال جمع أصل وأصل جمع أصيل فهو جمع الجمع مأخوذ من الأصل

TABRISI:13:12-15/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:12-15/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:12-15/r18.claim: Āṣāʾil is also used as a plural for the late-afternoon period.

TABRISI:13:12-15/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:12-15/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:12-15/r19.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb's poem uses aṣāʾil to mean the late-afternoon times.

TABRISI:13:12-15/r29.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:12-15/r29.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:12-15/r29.claim: The verbal nouns ṭawʿan and karhan are used in the place of circumstantial expressions.
TABRISI:13:12-15/r29.anchor: وطوعا وكرها مصدران وضعا موضع الحال

TABRISI:13:14-15/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:14-15/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:14-15/r6.claim: Those who prostrate to God are the angels and all morally responsible creatures.
TABRISI:13:14-15/r6.anchor: { ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض } يعني الملائكة وسائر المكلفين

TABRISI:13:14-15/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:14-15/r7.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد
TABRISI:13:14-15/r7.claim: Believers prostrate willingly, whereas unbelievers are compelled to prostrate at swordpoint.
TABRISI:13:14-15/r7.anchor: أحدهما: أن معناه أنه يجب السجود لله تعالى إلا أن المؤمن يسجد له طوعا والكافر يسجد له كرها بالسيف

TABRISI:13:14-15/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:14-15/r8.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:13:14-15/r8.claim: Another view says the verse means submission: believers submit willingly, while unbelievers are forced by pain and illness and cannot avoid submission to God.
TABRISI:13:14-15/r8.anchor: والثاني: أن المعنى ولله يخضع من في السماوات والأرض إلا أن المؤمن يخضع له طوعا

TABRISI:13:14-15/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:14-15/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:14-15/r9.claim: Their shadows also prostrate; on one view the shadow means the person, whose shadow accompanies him in prostration.
TABRISI:13:14-15/r9.anchor: قيل إن المراد بالظل الشخص فإن من يسجد يسجد ظله معه

TABRISI:13:14-15/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:14-15/r10.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:13:14-15/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan says an unbeliever's shadow prostrates though the unbeliever does not; in precise terms the body submits but the heart does not intend worship of God, prostrating from fear.
TABRISI:13:14-15/r10.anchor: قال الحسن يسجد ظل الكافر ولا يسجد الكافر ومعناه عند أهل التحقيق أنه يسجد شخصه دون قلبه

TABRISI:13:14-15/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:14-15/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:13:14-15/r11.claim: On the literal reading, shadows' prostration is their swaying from side to side and submission through being lengthened or shortened by God's command.
TABRISI:13:14-15/r11.anchor: وقيل إن الظلال على ظاهرها والمعنى في سجودها تمايلها من جانب إلى جانب

THALABI:v5p282/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p282/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p282/r1.claim: The beings in the heavens and earth who prostrate to God are the angels and believers.
THALABI:v5p282/r1.anchor: ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض يعني الملائكة والمؤمنين

THALABI:v5p282/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p282/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p282/r2.claim: Voluntary prostration belongs to believers; involuntary prostration belongs to hypocrites and disbelievers compelled to bow.
THALABI:v5p282/r2.anchor: طوعا وكرها يعني المنافقين والكافرين الذين أكرهوا على السجود بالسبعة

THALABI:v5p282#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p282#2/r1.speaker: ربيع بن هشيم
THALABI:v5p282#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Mubārak reports from Sufyān that Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym, on reciting the verse, would pray to God that he himself might prostrate willingly.
THALABI:v5p282#2/r1.anchor: وروى ابن المبارك عن سفيان قال: كان ربيع بن هشيم إذا قرأ هذه الآية

THALABI:v5p282#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p282#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p282#2/r2.claim: The shadows of those prostrating, willingly or under compulsion, incline to God as the person's shadow falls to the right or left.
THALABI:v5p282#2/r2.anchor: وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال يعني ضلال الساجدين طوعا أو كرها يسجد لله حين يقي ضلل أحدهم عن يمينه أو شماله

THALABI:v5p282#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p282#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p282#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this verse is paralleled in al-Naḥl.
THALABI:v5p282#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نظيرها في النحل

THALABI:v5p282#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p282#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v5p282#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī says that when a person prostrates at dawn or evening, the person's shadow prostrates with them.
THALABI:v5p282#2/r4.anchor: قال الكلبي: إذا سجد بالغدو أو العشي سجد معه ظله

THALABI:v5p282#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p282#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v5p282#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid says a believer's shadow prostrates willingly with its owner, while a disbeliever's shadow prostrates willingly even though its owner resists.
THALABI:v5p282#2/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ظل المؤمن يسجد طوعا وهو طائع

THALABI:v5p282#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p282#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p282#2/r6.claim: Āṣāl is the plural of aṣl, itself the plural of aṣīl, meaning late afternoon from the ʿaṣr prayer until sunset.
THALABI:v5p282#2/r6.anchor: والآصال جمع أصل، والأصل جمع الأصيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد والفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r1.claim: One reported reading says believers and angels prostrate willingly, while unbelievers do so under compulsion, such as threat of the sword.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r1.anchor: وهذا معنى قول الحسن (¬1)، وقتادة (¬2)، وابن زيد (¬3)، ونحو هذا قال الفراء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r2.claim: Al-Farra counts angels and those who enter Islam willingly or are born Muslim among the willing; a person forced into Islam prostrates unwillingly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r2.anchor: قال الفراء (¬4)، الساجد طوعا من أهل السموات والأرض: الملائكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r3.claim: The author says this account does not explain the whole verse, since it covers everyone on earth and not all unbelievers prostrate under coercion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r3.anchor: وهذا القدر لا يفتح معنى الآية؛ لأن قوله: {في السماوات والأرض} يقع على كل من في الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري عن بعض أهل العلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r4.claim: One specification confines unwilling prostration to unbelievers and hypocrites who fear being killed while inwardly retaining disbelief; angels and the righteous prostrate willingly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r4.anchor: حكى ابن الأنباري عن بعض أهل العلم (¬6) قال: الملائكة وعباد الله الصالحون يسجدون لله طوعا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r5.claim: Some interpreters apply unwillingness to believers who struggle to perform worship, compelling themselves while remaining Muslim and turning toward obedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r5.anchor: ومن المفسرين من ذهب إلى أن الكره أيضا من صفة المؤمنين، يسجد لله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r6.speaker: آخرون من المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r6.claim: Another view says sincere Muslims prostrate willingly and some Muslims do so reluctantly at first, until they become accustomed to the truth; this excludes unbelievers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: يسجد المخلصون لله طوعا، وبعض المسلمين كرها في ابتداء أمره، إلى أن يألف الحق، فعلى هذا لا مدخل للكافرين في الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r7.claim: A general reading takes prostration as obligatory: believers perform it willingly, while unbelievers are compelled to perform it as a legal ruling.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r7.anchor: المعنى على ما ذكره المفسرون: أن السجود واجب لله تعالى، فالمؤمن يفعله طوعا، والكافر يؤخذ بالسجود كرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r8.claim: On that general legal reading, “prostrates” reports voluntary worship but implies that unbelievers are ordered and compelled to prostrate; the author finds this wording unlikely.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r9.speaker: أصحاب المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r9.claim: The semanticists read unbelievers’ prostration figuratively as their submission to God’s control over health, sickness, wealth, poverty, life, and death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r9.anchor: سجود الكافر هو تذلله وانقياده لتصريف الله تعالى إياه فيما يريد من عافية إلى مرض، وغنى إلى فقر، وحياة إلى موت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r10.speaker: أصحاب المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r10.claim: This figurative submission resembles the statement that all in the heavens and earth are obedient to God, and that all submit to Him willingly or unwillingly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p326/r10.anchor: ونظير هذه الآية قوله تعالى: {بل له ما في السماوات والأرض كل له قانتون} [البقرة: 116]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r1.claim: The commentators say every person’s shadow, whether the person is a believer or unbeliever, prostrates to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: كل شخص مؤمن أو كافر، فإنه يسجد لله تعالى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r2.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r2.claim: Mujahid says a believer’s shadow prostrates willingly while he obeys, whereas an unbeliever’s shadow does so willingly while he himself is reluctant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد (¬2): ظل المؤمن يسجد طوعا وهو طائع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq reports an interpretation that an unbeliever worships something other than God while his shadow prostrates to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r3.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق (¬3): جاء في التفسير أن الكافر يسجد لغير الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r4.claim: On that interpretation, shadows are given minds with which to prostrate and humble themselves, just as mountains are given understanding; most exegetes follow this approach.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r4.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري (¬4): يجعل للظلال عقول تسجد بها وتخشع، كما جعل للجبال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r5.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r5.claim: The semanticists explain shadow-prostration as their leaning and turning from side to side, lengthening as the sun descends and shortening as it rises; this is submission to God’s control.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r5.anchor: سجود الظلال ميلانها ودورانها من جانبها إلى جانب، وطولها بانحطاط الشمس، وقصرها بارتفاع الشمس فهي مستسلمة منقادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r6.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r6.claim: In Arabic, prostration can mean inclination: a palm tree is said to prostrate when its heavy fruit makes it bend; Labid’s verse supplies the usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p328/r6.anchor: والميل سجود في اللغة، يقال: سجدت النخلة، إذا مالت (¬5) لكثرة حملها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:15/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:15/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:15/r1.claim: Those who prostrate willingly are the angels and believers.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:15/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:15/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:15/r2.claim: Those compelled to prostrate do so out of fear of the sword; although the wording is general, its intended referent is specific.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:15/r2.anchor: وهم من أكرهوا على السجود، فسجدوا لله سبحانه من خوف السيف، واللفظ عام والمراد به الخصوص

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:15/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:15/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:15/r3.claim: Every person's shadow, believer or disbeliever, prostrates morning and evening; people do not know how this occurs.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:15/r3.anchor: كل شخص مؤمن أو كافر فإن ظله يسجد لله، ونحن لا نقف على كيفية ذلك

QASHANI:13:15-17/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:15-17/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:15-17/r1.claim: Those in the heavens and earth are spiritual realities; their shadows are the bodies and forms that serve as their images.
QASHANI:13:15-17/r1.anchor: { ولله } ينقاد { من في السموات والأرض } من الحقائق الروحانيات كأعيان الجواهر وملكوت الأشياء

QASHANI:13:15-17/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:15-17/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:15-17/r2.claim: Their bodily forms and psychic images are shadows of spiritual realities, as the Prophet's prostration prayer also indicates.
QASHANI:13:15-17/r2.anchor: ولهذا قرأ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذه السجدة:

QASHANI:13:15-17/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:15-17/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:15-17/r3.claim: The prayer's face, shadow, and imagination signify essential reality, bodily person, and psychic image: being, identity, and individual form.
QASHANI:13:15-17/r3.anchor: أي: حقيقة ذاتي وسواد شخصي وخيال نفسي، أي: وجودي وعيني وشخصي

QASHANI:13:15-17/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:15-17/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:15-17/r4.claim: All must submit whether they will or not, although some submit willingly and others reluctantly.
QASHANI:13:15-17/r4.anchor: { طوعا وكرها } أي: شاؤوا أو أبوا، والمعنى يلزمهم ذلك اضطرارا

QASHANI:13:15-17/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:15-17/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:15-17/r5.claim: The phrase means their submission is continual.

ELMALILI:13:15/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:15/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:15/r1.claim: Here prostration means bowing down and submitting in obedience.
ELMALILI:13:15/r1.anchor: secde eder boyun eğer, inkıyad eyler

ELMALILI:13:15/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:15/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:15/r2.claim: Those in the heavens may mean angels, or intellects, spirits, and lofty faculties in the higher realms.
ELMALILI:13:15/r2.anchor: melâike veya yukarı makamlarda bulunan ukūl u ervâh

ELMALILI:13:15/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:15/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:15/r3.claim: Those on earth may mean humanity and jinn, the two weighty species generally, or lower souls.
ELMALILI:13:15/r3.anchor: yerdeki kimseler yani umûmiyetle ins ü cin, sekaleyn, veya aşağıda bulunan nüfûs-ı sâfile

ELMALILI:13:15/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:15/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:15/r4.claim: All submit whether willingly or unwillingly, voluntarily or under compulsion.
ELMALILI:13:15/r4.anchor: gerek tav‘an ve gerek kerhen ister istemez

ELMALILI:13:15/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:15/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:15/r5.claim: Their shadows also prostrate morning and evening; if the people themselves do not submit willingly, their shadows submit under compulsion to God's command, not their owners'.
ELMALILI:13:15/r5.anchor: gölgeleri de tav‘an değilse kerhen ve bi’l-mecbûriye Allah’a secde ederler. Gölgelerin bile yerlere kapanışı sâhiplerinin değil, Allah’ın emrine inkıyaddır

ELMALILI:13:15/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:15/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:15/r6.claim: The verse may also hint that bodies are like shadows in relation to intellects and spirits, since spirits are luminous while bodies are dark.
ELMALILI:13:15/r6.anchor: Burada ukūl ü ervâh mukabilinde ebdân ü ecsâmın birer gölge mesâbesinde olduğuna da işaret vardır denebilir. Zira ervâh nûrânî, ecsâm zulmânîdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r1.claim: Prostration means worship and submission; voluntary prostration belongs to humans, who freely obey God and thereby earn reward.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r1.anchor: Birincisi insanlara mahsus olup insanlar serbest iradeleriyle Allah’a secde yani itaat ederek bununla sevap kazanırlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r2.claim: In the compulsory sense, all beings—including humans, animals, plants, and inanimate things—prostrate to God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r2.anchor: insan, hayvan, bitki ve cansız varlıkların tamamı Allah’a secde etmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r3.claim: Willing or unwilling prostration means God's rule applies to everything and nothing escapes his will, command, or laws; even unbelievers must submit to natural law.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r3.anchor: Allah’ın hükmünün her şey için geçerli olduğunu, hiçbir şeyin O’nun iradesi, buyruğu ve kanunlarının dışına çıkamayacağını belirtir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r4.claim: Shadows prostrate morning and evening as the sun makes them stretch west in the morning, shorten or disappear at noon, then stretch east later.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r4.anchor: sabahları batıya doğru uzaması, öğle vaktinde sıfırlanması veya en kısa haline gelmesi öğle-akşam arasında doğuya doğru uzamasıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r5.claim: The changing shadows are likened to a person bowing in prostration; their movement expresses creation's submission to God's order and natural laws.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r5.anchor: Âyet-i kerîmede gölgelerin bu durumu, secdeye kapanan insanın durumuna benzetilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r6.claim: Another verse says that the shadows of God's created things contract, turn right and left, and prostrate to him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:15/r6.anchor: aynı mânada bir başka âyet-i kerîmede Allah’ın yarattığı varlıkların gölgelerinin küçülerek ve Allah’a secde ederek sağa sola döndüğü ifade edilmiştir

QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r10.speaker: أهل التفسير
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r10.claim: Exegetes say the believer prostrates to God voluntarily, while affliction forces the believer to humble themself; this is the meaning of prostrating under compulsion.
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r10.anchor: المؤمن يسجد لله طوعا ، وإذا نزل به ضر ألجأه إلى أن يتواضع ويسجد ، وذلك معنى سجوده كرها - وهذا قول أهل التفسير

QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r11.claim: A disbeliever may prostrate willingly to seek relief from harm, but this too counts as compelled prostration; likewise, prostration for reward or to remove an ordeal is directed by need.
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r11.anchor: والكافر يسجد طائعا مختارا ، ولكن لما كان سجوده لطلب كشف الضر قال تعالى

QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r12.claim: Prostration has two kinds: prostration of the self, which is familiar, and prostration of the heart, which belongs to spiritual presence.
QUSHAYRI:v2p102/r12.anchor: ويقال السجود على قسمين : ساجد بنفسه وساجد بقلبه ؛ فسجود النفس معهود ، وسجود القلب من حيث الوجود

BURHAN:v4p411/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p411/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p411/r1.claim: The noun man can function as subject, object, or topic and has four agreed categories: relative, interrogative, conditional, and indefinite qualified by a following clause.
BURHAN:v4p411/r1.anchor: لا تكون إلا اسما لوقوعها فاعلة ومفعولة ومبتدأة ولها اربعة اقسام متفق عليها

BURHAN:v4p411/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p411/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p411/r2.claim: As a relative pronoun, man appears in the statements that whoever is in the heavens and earth belongs to God and that whoever is there prostrates to Him.
BURHAN:v4p411/r2.anchor: ﴿ ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض ﴾

SULAMI:v1p330/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p330/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p330/r1.claim: The knower prostrates willingly, while the heedless person does so reluctantly.
SULAMI:v1p330/r1.anchor: قال الجنيد : العارف طوعا ، والمعرض كرها .

SULAMI:v1p330/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p330/r2.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p330/r2.claim: When calamities descend, the person is humbled; when hope comes, he grows proud.
SULAMI:v1p330/r2.anchor: قال الجنيد : العارف طوعا ، والمعرض كرها . وقال إذا نزلته المصائب ذل ، وإذا جاءه الرجاء مل .

AKHFASH:v2p403/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p403/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p403/r1.claim: Ghuduww denotes morning though it is morphologically a verb; ibkār derives from abkara, while some explain al-abkār as the plural of bakr.
AKHFASH:v2p403/r1.anchor: وقال {بالغدو والآصال} و {بالعشي والإبكار} فجعل "الغدو" يدل على الغداة

AKHFASH:v2p403/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p403/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p403/r2.claim: He rejects pluralizing bakr as abkār because bakr is an indeclinable noun and a verbal noun like ibkār; the alternative claims the forms are plurals of bakra and ghudwa, but faʿla does not pluralize as afʿāl.
AKHFASH:v2p403/r2.anchor: لانه اسم ليس بمتمكن وهو أيضا مصدر مثل "الإبكار"

DAMGHANI:v1p306/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p306/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p306/r3.claim: Al-ẓill can mean shade from a tree, wall, or other object; compare Moses’ retreat to shade.
DAMGHANI:v1p306/r3.anchor: الثاني الظل يعني للشجرة والحائط كقوله سبحانه في سورة الرعد

DAMGHANI:v1p229/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p229/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p229/r11.claim: The five-sense list for sujūd includes prayer, prophets, submission, bowing, and prostration itself; here prayer is illustrated.
DAMGHANI:v1p229/r11.anchor: س ج د على خمسة أوجه الصلاة الأنبياء الانقياد الركوع السجود بعينه

FARRA:v2p60/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p60/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p60/r5.claim: The angels prostrate willingly; people who embrace or are born into Islam do so willingly, while one compelled into Islam prostrates reluctantly.
FARRA:v2p60/r5.anchor: فالملائكة تسجد طوعا، ومن دخل في الإسلام رغبة فيه أو ولد عليه من أهل الأرض فهو أيضا طائع.

FARRA:v2p60/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p60/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p60/r6.claim: Each person's shadow prostrates with him morning and evening; as it inclines in the evening it becomes fayʾ, and singular and plural are equivalent in sense here.
FARRA:v2p60/r6.anchor: كل شخص فظله بالغداة والعشي يسجد معه. لأن الظل يفيء بالعشي فيصير فيئا يسجد.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p226#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p226#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p226#3/r1.claim: Sujūd willingly or unwillingly means surrendering, yielding, and submitting.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p226#3/r1.anchor: {ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها} أي: يستسلم وينقاد ويخضع.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237/r2.claim: Angels in heaven and believers on earth submit willingly; earthly unbelievers submit unwillingly from fear of the sword.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237/r2.anchor: أي يستسلم من في السموات من الملائكة، ومن في الأرض من المؤمنين طوعا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237/r3.claim: The shadows submit in the morning and evening, just as all in the heavens and earth submit in 3:83.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237/r3.anchor: وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال مستسلمة. وهو مثل قوله: وله أسلم من في السماوات والأرض

MAJAZ:v1p327/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p327/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p327/r2.claim: Al-āṣāl means evenings; its singular is aṣl, and aṣīl is the time from midafternoon to sunset. Abū Dhuʾayb and al-Nābighah’s poems illustrate the forms.
MAJAZ:v1p327/r2.anchor: «بالغدو والآصال» (15) أي بالعشي، واحدها: أصل وواحد الأصل أصيل وهو ما بين العصر إلى مغرب الشمس

NAHHAS:v2p355/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p355/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p355/r1.claim: Al-Nahhas prefers prostration here as submission to God's governance and changes, including health and illness.
NAHHAS:v2p355/r1.anchor: ومن أحسن ما قيل أن السجود ههنا الخضوع لتدبير الله جل وعز وتصريفه من صحة وسقم وغيرهما

NAHHAS:v2p355/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p355/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p355/r2.claim: People submit willingly or unwillingly, with no escape; their shadows submit as the sun lengthens and shortens them through time.
NAHHAS:v2p355/r2.anchor: أي ينقادون على ما أحبوا أو كرهوا لا حيلة لهم في ذلك وظلالهم أيضا منقادة لتدبير الله جل وعز

SAMIN-DURR:13:15/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:15/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:15/r1.claim: طوعا وكرها can be a causal accusative, a circumstantial accusative meaning willing and unwilling, or an emphatic verbal noun with an implicit verb.
SAMIN-DURR:13:15/r1.anchor: { طوعا وكرها }: إما مفعول من أجله، وإما حال، أي: طائعين وكارهين، وإما منصوب على المصدر المؤكد

SAMIN-DURR:13:15/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:15/r2.speaker: أبو مجلز
SAMIN-DURR:13:15/r2.claim: Abu Mujliz reads والإيصال, adding yāʾ before ṣād.
SAMIN-DURR:13:15/r2.anchor: وقرأ ألو مجلز: " والإيصال " بالياء قبل الصاد.

SAMIN-DURR:13:15/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:15/r3.speaker: ابن جني
SAMIN-DURR:13:15/r3.claim: Ibn Jinni parses أبو مجلز's form as the verbal noun of آصل, meaning to enter the evening, by analogy with أصبح, enter the morning.
SAMIN-DURR:13:15/r3.anchor: وخرجها ابن جني على أنه مصدر " آصل " كضارب، أي: دخل في الأصيل، كأصبح،

SAMIN-DURR:13:15/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:15/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:15/r5.claim: بالغدو depends on يسجد, and the preposition ب means في: in these two periods.
SAMIN-DURR:13:15/r5.anchor: " بالغدو " متعلق بيسجد، والباء بمعنى في، أي: في هذين الوقتين.

ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r5.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r5.claim: One reported interpretation says believers prostrate willingly and unbelievers unwillingly.
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r5.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن المؤمن يسجد طوعا

ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r6.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r6.claim: Another report says some people entered Islam willingly, while others did so only after being threatened with a sword and initially submitted unwillingly.
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r6.anchor: وجاء أن من الناس من دخل في الإسلام طوعا ومنهم من لم يدخل

ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r7.claim: Zajjāj allows that prostration means submission: some accept God's command when easy, while others accept even what they find burdensome.
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r7.anchor: وجائز - والله أعلم - أن يكون (طوعا وكرها)

ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r8.claim: The shadows also prostrate to God.
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r8.anchor: أي وتسجد ظلالهم. وجاء في التفسير أن الكافر

ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r9.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r9.claim: A reported explanation says that unbelievers prostrate to other gods while their shadows prostrate to God.
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r9.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن الكافر يسجد لغير الله

ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r10.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r10.claim: A view takes their shadows to mean their bodies, which Zajjāj says conflicts with the interpretation.
ZAJJAJ:v3p143/r10.anchor: وقيل وظلالهم أشخاصهم، وهذا مخالف للتفسير

ASAD-NOTES:13:15#n33/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:15#n33/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:13:15#n33/r1.claim: Yasjud is a metonym for complete submission to God's will, understood here as submission to the natural laws He decreed.
ASAD-NOTES:13:15#n33/r1.anchor: yasjud ("prostrates himself" or "prostrate themselves") is a metonym for complete submission to His will (Zamakhshari)

ASAD-NOTES:13:15#n33/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:15#n33/r2.speaker: most of the classical commentators
ASAD-NOTES:13:15#n33/r2.claim: They identify willing submitters as angels and believers, while deniers unwillingly remain subject to God's will without knowing it.
ASAD-NOTES:13:15#n33/r2.anchor: According to most of the classical commentators, those who submit to God willingly (i.e., consciously) are the angels and the believers

ASAD-NOTES:13:15#n33/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:15#n33/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:13:15#n33/r3.claim: Because shadows are mentioned next, Asad takes man to include all physical things, animate and inanimate, not only conscious beings.
ASAD-NOTES:13:15#n33/r3.anchor: it is logical to assume that the relative pronoun man relates in this context not merely to conscious beings but also to all other physical objects

ASAD-NOTES:13:15#n34/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:15#n34/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:13:15#n34/r1.claim: A material object's shadow changes with the sun's position; its morning and evening lengthening visibly expresses subjection to God's creative will.
ASAD-NOTES:13:15#n34/r1.anchor: varying lengths of the shadow projected by any material object depend on the position of the sun in relation to the earth

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#5/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#5/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#5/r4.claim: The general statement that all in heaven and earth prostrate in 13:15 leaves من unrepeated; 22:18 repeats it while listing celestial and terrestrial beings in detail.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#5/r4.anchor: فلم يكرر الموصول في حين قال:

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p488/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p488/r1.speaker: قالوا
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p488/r1.claim: They explain benefit preceding harm in 13:16 by its preceding order طوعاً وكرهاً in 13:15; in Sabaʾ, benefit precedes harm after mention of God’s expanding provision.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p488/r1.anchor: فقدّم النفع على الضرر، قالوا: وذلك لتقدم قوله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p888/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p888/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p888/r2.claim: من denotes rational beings and possessors of knowledge; ما can denote their qualities and nonrational things, making it broader. Since willing and unwilling are qualities of rational beings, 13:15 uses من.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p888/r2.anchor: والطوع والكره من صفات العقلاء فاستعمل (من)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Everything obeys God by its existence; people who misuse their choice still live within His law, and arrogance rebels against their own nature.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: everything by its actual existence obeys God. If they who have been given some freedom of choice misuse this freedom

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Shadows illustrate subjection to God’s law: they prostrate at night, rise slowly at dawn, then prostrate again as the sun descends at midday.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: even the shadows of things prostrate at night and slowly lift their heads at dawn

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The shadow image is insinuative reasoning: it directs the mind to a symbol’s reality through human nature rather than formal logic.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This is a special form of reasoning called insinuation. In it, attention of the mind is directed to the reality of a symbol.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r1.claim: If prostration means submission, everyone obeys God's will whether willing or unwilling; shadows likewise follow his will in lengthening, shrinking, and disappearing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r1.anchor: إن كان السجود بمعنى الخضوع والانقياد، فمن عمومها ينقاد كلهم إلى ما أراده تعالى بهم شاؤوا أو أبوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r2.claim: Qatada takes coerced converts as prostrating unwillingly, perhaps hypocritically or only at first, before their faith becomes genuine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r2.anchor: وبالكره عن سجود من ضمه السيف إلى الإسلام كما قاله قتادة: فيسجد كرها وإما نفاقا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r3.claim: On the bodily-prostration reading, the verse is general but excludes those who do not prostrate; willing prostration belongs to angels and believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r3.anchor: وإن كان السجود عبارة عن الهيئة المخصوصة: وهو وضع الجبهة بالمكان الذي يكون فيه الواضع، فيكون عاما مخصوصا إذ يخرج منه من لا يسجد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r4.claim: Another view calls prostration voluntary when it is not burdensome, and compelled when religious duties make it difficult.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r4.anchor: وقيل: طوعا لا يثقل عليه السجود، وكرها يثقل عليه، لأن إلزام التكاليف مشقة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says long-established Muslims prostrate willingly from habit, while new Muslims do so unwillingly until accustomed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r5.anchor: وكرها من بدا بالإسلام إلى أن يألف السجود قاله ابن الأنباري.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r6.claim: A bodily reading can be general if يسجد is formally indicative but denotes the result, or if it expresses an obligation to prostrate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r6.anchor: وذلك بأن يكون يسجد صيغته صيغة الخبر، ومدلوله أثر. أو يكون معناه: يجب أن يسجد له كل من في السموات والأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r7.claim: The passage's thrust is that all creation is dominated by God and confined to his will, including the beings people worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r7.anchor: والذي يظهر أن مساق هذه الآية إنما هو أن العالم كله مقهور لله تعالى، خاضع لما أراد منه، مقصور على مشيئته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r8.claim: Including shadows shows the verse is not only about physical posture: shadows are not persons, but are governed by God's will as part of creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r8.anchor: والظلال ليست أشخاصا يتصور منها السجود بالهيئة المخصوصة، ولكنها داخلة تحت مشيئته تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r9.claim: The author links shadows bowing here to the verse that says shadows move from right and left in prostration to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r9.anchor: كما قال تعالى: أولم يروا إلى ما خلق الله من شيء يتفيؤا ظلاله عن اليمين والشمائل سجدا لله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r10.claim: He rejects taking shadows to mean people, and more strongly rejects Ibn al-Anbari's idea that shadows have minds that prostrate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r10.anchor: وكون الظلال يراد بها الأشخاص كما قال بعضهم ضعيف، وأضعف منه قول ابن الأنباري: أنه تعالى جعل للظلال عقولا تسجد بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r11.claim: Shadow-prostration means shadows incline from one side to another as God wills; shadows are accidents that cannot possess life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p368/r11.anchor: وأما الظل فعرض لا يتصور قيام الحياة به، وإنما معنى سجود الظلال ميلها من جانب إلى جانب كما أراد تعالى.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r1.claim: Al-Alūsī takes سجود as humility and submission: all creation is subject to God's decrees alone. Fronting لله gives exclusivity, ruling out any independent or shared submission to another.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r1.anchor: يخضع وينقاد لا لشيء غيره سبحانه استقلالا ولا اشتراكا فالقصر ينتظم القلب والإفراد

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r2.claim: On the apparent reading, من denotes angels and the two rational kinds, humans and jinn; they are singled out as central, and their submission demonstrates that of other beings. Alternatively it includes nonrational creation too, with من used by predominance.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r2.anchor: من الملائكة والثقلين كما يقتضيه ظاهر التعبير بمن

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r3.claim: The accusatives may be circumstantial adverbs; if a verbal noun cannot directly function as a state, understand them as طائعين وكارهين.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r3.anchor: نصب على الحال فان قلنا بوقوع المصدر حالا من غير تأويل فهو ظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r4.claim: All submit to God's greatness and to the coming of His decrees of creation and annihilation, willingly or unwillingly, without another authority intervening in any of it.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r4.anchor: من غير مداخلة حكم غيره جل وعلا بل غير حكمه تعالى في شيء من ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r5.claim: Another parse makes the words causal accusatives; كره then means compulsion, a passive verbal noun so its agent matches the subject of prostration, while grammarians who do not require matching can retain its ordinary sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r5.anchor: وجوز أن يكون النصب على العلة فالكره بمعنى الإكراه وهو مصدر المبني للمفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r6.claim: Al-Alūsī answers that unwillingness can still be a cause: a cause is whatever prompts an act or results from it, not only an intended goal; the accusatives may alternatively be objects of absolute verbal force, سجود طوع وكره.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r6.anchor: وما قيل عليه من أن اعتبار العلية في الكره غير ظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r7.claim: Their shadows may mean those belonging to earthly beings alone, or to them and every dense body; al-Shihāb's marginal note advises referring the pronoun to earth-dwellers, since heavenly beings have no shadow absent metonymy or an inclusive reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r7.anchor: وفي الحواشي الشهابية ينبغي أن يرجع الضمير لمن في الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r8.claim: A shadow's submission consists in following God's will as He extends and contracts it, makes it recede, or causes it to disappear.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r8.anchor: ومعنى انقياد الظلال له تعالى أنها تابعة لتصرفه سبحانه ومشيئته في الامتداد والتقلص

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r9.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says ẓill was originally a verbal noun and then came to denote the image cast by a body, whether reversed or upright; further implications are discussed elsewhere.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126/r9.anchor: وأصل الظل كما قال الفراء مصدر ثم أطلق على الخيال الذي يظهر للجرم

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r1.claim: The phrase is temporal for an implicit سجود, with باء meaning في; morning and evening stand for continuous submission. If it modifies the shadows, their movement is especially visible at those times.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r1.anchor: ظرف للسجود المقدر والباء بمعنى في وهو كثير والمراد بهما الدوام

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r2.claim: Ghuduww is the plural of ghadāh; āṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, the interval between afternoon and sunset, though it is also analyzed as a plural of aṣl from aṣīl with its second hamza changed to alif.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r2.anchor: والآصال جمع أصيل وهو مابين العصر والمغرب

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r3.speaker: ابن مجلز
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r3.claim: Ibn Mujliz reads الإيصال with kasra on the hamza, treating it as the verbal noun of آصلنا, “we entered the evening,” as Ibn Jinnī explains.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r3.anchor: بقراءة ابن مجلز ( الإيصال ) بكسر الهمزة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r4.claim: Some take prostration literally: unbelievers single out God in worship when forced by distress, as in the verse about people at sea calling on Him with sincere devotion.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : إن المراد حقيقة السجود فإن الكفرة حالة الاضطرار

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī suggests God may create understanding in shadows so they prostrate, as He did in mountains so they glorified Him and showed effects of divine manifestation.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r5.anchor: ولا يبعد أن يخلق الله تعالى في الظلال إفهاما وعقولا بها تسجد

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r6.claim: Another view takes the shadows' prostration as the visible posture of their owners; this requires a broad metaphor, an implied causative, or a defense that incidental metaphor or combining literal and figurative senses is permissible, with some options problematic.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r6.anchor: عموم المجاز في السجود المذكور في الآية بأن يراد به الوقوع

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r7.claim: Qatāda reads سجود as the bodily posture: angels and believers prostrate willingly, while those brought into Islam under the sword do so unwillingly, whether hypocritically or because compulsion marked their first state.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r7.anchor: وعن قتادة أن السجود عبارة عن الهيئة المخصوصة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r8.claim: Another view calls willing those for whom prostration is easy and unwilling those who find it burdensome.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r9.claim: Since some beings do not prostrate, one view makes من general in wording but restricted in intended scope; another includes every rational being and takes يسجد as “must prostrate,” emphatically expressing obligation as occurrence.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r9.anchor: والمراد بيسجد يجب أن يسجد لكن عبر عن الوجوب بالوقوع مبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r10.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r10.claim: Al-Alūsī favors the cosmic-submission reading: the whole world, including shadows, is governed by God's will, so the beings worshipped by polytheists can neither harm nor benefit anyone.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r10.anchor: واختار غير واحد في تفسير الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r11.speaker: الإرشاد
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r11.claim: Al-Irshād argues that an idolater's prostration to God only in distress cannot establish the verse's exclusivity, since the same person worships idols in ease; universal submission through creation and annihilation is a stronger rebuke.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r11.anchor: وفي إرشاد العقل السليم بعد نقل ما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r12.claim: Al-Alūsī rejects Ibn al-Anbārī's analogy: a mountain could have intellect if granted life, but a shadow is an accident incapable of life; its prostration is its shifting between sides and changing as God wills.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p126#2/r12.anchor: الجبل يمكن أن يكون له عقل بشرط تقدير الحياة وأما الظل فعرض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r1.claim: Angels and believers prostrate willingly; hypocrites and disbelievers do so unwillingly, compelled by the sword.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r1.anchor: طوعا} يعني: الملائكة والمؤمنين، {وكرها} يعني: المنافقين والكافرين الذين أكرهوا على السجود بالسيف.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r2.claim: The shadows of those who prostrate willingly or unwillingly themselves prostrate willingly to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r2.anchor: {وظلالهم} يعني: ظلال الساجدين طوعا وكرها تسجد لله عز وجل طوعا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says a believer's shadow prostrates willingly along with him, while a disbeliever's shadow does so willingly though he resists.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد: ظل المؤمن يسجد طوعا وهو طائع، وظل الكافر يسجد طوعا وهو كاره.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r4.claim: A shadow prostrates with its person at dawn or evening; al-asal is the plural of al-asīl, the time from afternoon prayer until sunset.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r4.anchor: {بالغدو والآصال} يعني إذا سجد بالغدو أو العشي يسجد معه ظله. و"الآصال": جمع "الأصل"، و"الأصل" جمع "الأصيل"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r5.claim: Another view takes their shadows to mean their persons and the times as mornings and evenings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: ظلالهم أي: أشخاصهم، بالغدو والآصال: بالبكر والعشايا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r6.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r6.claim: A further explanation is that a shadow's prostration means its being subdued to the purpose for which it was made.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p306#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: سجود الظل تذليله لما أريد له.

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r1.claim: Prostration may be literal: angels and believing humans prostrate willingly in hardship and ease, while unbelievers do so unwillingly under hardship and necessity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r1.anchor: فإنه يسجد له الملائكة والمؤمنون من الثقلين

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r2.claim: Alternatively, the prostration means that people submit to God's bringing about what He wills in them, whether they wish it or not, while their shadows submit to His extending and contracting them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r2.anchor: وأن يراد به انقيادهم لإحداث ما أراده منهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r3.claim: طوعا وكرها may be circumstantial accusatives or express the cause of prostration.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r3.anchor: وانتصاب { طوعا وكرها } بالحال أو العلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r4.claim: The time phrase may modify يسجد or describe the shadows; the two times can imply permanence, and are specified because shadows grow long and numerous then.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r4.anchor: والمراد بهما الدوام أو حال من الظلال

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r5.claim: غدو is the plural of غداة, like قنى from قناة; الآصال is the plural of أصيل, the time between afternoon and sunset. Another reading is الإيصال, entering the evening.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:15/r5.anchor: والغدو جمع غداة كقنى جمع قناة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r1.claim: After describing God’s clear call by command in His books, Biqaʿi explains the call by decree through the submission of all creation, recalling 11:119.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r2.claim: Sujūd means submission, compliance, and humility, as in the discussion of differing people and divine mercy at 11:119.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r2.anchor: أي يخضع وينقاد ويتذلل كما بين عند قوله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r3.claim: Everything in heaven and earth submits to God's operative judgments and decrees.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r4.claim: Voluntary submission is compliance with a command that the self is invited to obey.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r4.anchor: والطوع : الانقياد للأمر الذي يدعى إليه من قبل النفس

BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r5.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r5.claim: Al-Razi says even an unbeliever counts as prostrating in effect, though unwilling, because need compels submission.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r5.anchor: قال الرازي رحمه الله : والكافر في حكم الساجد وإن أباه لما به من الحاجة الداعية إلى الخضوع

BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r6.claim: Every kind of being, animate or inanimate, rational or not, spiritual or not, is humbled and governed by the Creator and Lord of command.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r6.anchor: سجود كل صنف هو تذلله وتسخره وانقياده

BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r7.speaker: الشيخ محيي الدين النووي
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r7.claim: Al-Nawawi says sujūd originally means humility and submission; every inanimate thing’s Quranic prostration is obedience to what it was made subject to, while placing the forehead down is the utmost form.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r7.anchor: وقال الشيخ محيي الدين النووي رضي الله عنه فس شرح المهذب

BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r8.claim: Shadows also submit because no one can change their spreading, shortening as the sun rises and lengthening as it declines.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r9.claim: Ghuduww is the plural of ghadāh, the early morning or first part of the day.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r9.anchor: جمع غداة , وهي البكرة : أول النهار

BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r10.claim: Āṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, generally the afternoon and in some places around midday; aṣīl is from mid-afternoon to sunset, the beginning from which night develops.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r10.anchor: جمع أصيل , دائما في جميع البلاد , وفي وسط النهار في بعض البلاد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r11.claim: A ẓill is the shade screening an object, while fayʾ is shade returning after the light has passed.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r11.anchor: والظل : ستر الشخص ما بإزائه , والفيء : الذي يرجع بعد ذهاب ضوئه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r12.claim: Biqaʿi traces ṣalā and its rearrangements to connection: prayer joins servant to Lord through supplication, pardon, mercy, divine praise, or formal prayer; the excerpt then begins further bodily and horse-related senses.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r12.anchor: ومادة ( صلا ) - واوية ويائية مهموزة وغير مهموزة بتراكيبها الأحد عشر

BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r13.claim: Other derivatives of ṣalā include the middle of the back or hindquarters and a pregnant camel’s loosened hindquarter; a musallī horse is the runner immediately behind the leader.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p135/r13.anchor: والصلا : وسط الظهر منا , أو من كل ذي أربع

BIQAI-FULL:v4p136/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p136/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p136/r1.claim: Biqāʿī traces صال to following or rushing upon with force, citing the donkey driving its mate and a man or stallion attacking; related forms can mean mixing or gathering what was scattered.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p136/r1.anchor: الذي يجيء عل إثر السابق , فإنه يواصله , وصلى الحمار أتنه : طردها وقحمها الطريق

BIQAI-FULL:v4p136/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p136/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p136/r2.claim: He gives union and joining as the semantic core of الوصلة, opposed to separation, and relates it to joints, joined things, relationships, and continuity.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p136/r2.anchor: والوصلة - التي هي مدار المادة وكأنها الحقيقة التي تشعبت منها فروعها - هي الضم وهي التئام الشيء بالشيء

BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r1.claim: He extends connection and continuity through وصيلة: a ewe bearing a male then a female, linked garments, entangled yarn, broad land, and the final night connecting two months.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r1.anchor: والوصيلة : الشاة تلد ذكرا ثم تلد أنثى , فتصل الظهر

BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r2.claim: Roasting is described as joining meat to fire; related forms mean casting into fire or heating a hand, while صليت فلانا means dealing with or deceiving him to secure his company.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r2.anchor: وصليت اللحم : شويته - لأنك وصلته بالنار

BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r3.claim: The forms for putting something into fire, heating a hand, and enduring its heat derive from joining the object to fire.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r3.anchor: وأصليته النار : أدخلته إياها وأثويته فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r4.claim: الصلاية means the forehead because it repeatedly touches the ground in prayer, and also a perfume-pounder because it is repeatedly used for pounding.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r4.anchor: والصلاية - ويهمز : الجبهة , لكثرة مباشرتها الأرض في الصلاة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r5.claim: A Prophetic report says Satan has snares and traps; Biqāʿī uses it to gloss مصالي as the plural of مصلاة, a snare, alongside فخ, a trap.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r5.anchor: ومنه الحديث ( إن للشيطان مصالي وفخوخا ) جمع مصلاة وفخ

BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r6.speaker: القزاز
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r6.claim: Al-Qazzāz describes al-ṣilyān as a plant with a large root, one of the best pastures, eaten by horses; Biqāʿī says it was named for camels’ frequent grazing on it.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r6.anchor: وقال القزاز : وهو شجر له جعثن ضخم , ربما جرد وسطه ونبت ما حوله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r7.speaker: القزاز
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r7.claim: A reported gloss says لصيت الرجل means to accuse or reproach someone with sexual wrongdoing, while لصي إليه means to join him under suspicion.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r7.anchor: ولصيت الرجل كرميت ورضيت - إذا عبته وقذفته بالفجور , وقال القزاز : وقيل : هو أن يضيفه إلى ربية

BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r8.claim: He records aṣla as a snake that attacks a person; the dictionaries differ on whether it is small or large, with the latter described as deadly by its breath.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r9.claim: Several side forms express assault or motion: a camel may attack people, and a horse’s neigh is called صئيل because its notes continue in sequence.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r9.anchor: وصؤل البعير - ككرم صآلة : واثب الناس أو صار يقتل الناس ويعدو عليهم , وصئيل الفرس : صهيله - لمواصلة نغماته

BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r10.claim: Aṣīl can denote someone of lineage, while aṣl is a foundation; the verb for becoming rooted also means becoming established or firm.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r11.claim: Al-aṣī means evening, either as the link between day and night or as night itself; alternatively it signals day’s end, as if the day were uprooted from its source. The term also extends to death and destruction.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r11.anchor: والأصي : العشي - لأنه وصلة ما بين النهار والليل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r12.claim: Biqāʿī says his earlier discussion of the wording “your prayer commands you” in Hūd signals the same lexical point.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p137/r12.anchor: وقد مضى عند قوله تعالى وفي سورة هود عليه السلام

DURR-FULL:v4p629/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the willing prostrator as the believer and the reluctant one as the unbeliever’s shadow.
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد - رضي الله عنه - في الآية قال الطائع المؤمن والكاره ظل الكافر

DURR-FULL:v4p629/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r4.claim: Mujahid says the believer’s shadow prostrates willingly and the unbeliever’s shadow reluctantly.
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد - رضي الله عنه - {ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال} قال: ظل المؤمن يسجد {طوعا} وهو طائع لله

DURR-FULL:v4p629/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r5.claim: Qatada says a believer prostrates willingly while an unbeliever does so reluctantly through his shadow.
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r5.anchor: عن قتادة - رضي الله عنه - {ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها} قال: أما المؤمن فيسجد طائعا

DURR-FULL:v4p629/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says those in heaven prostrate willingly, while those on earth do so both willingly and unwillingly.
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r6.anchor: يسجد من في السموات طوعا ومن في الأرض طوعا وكرها

DURR-FULL:v4p629/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd explains willingness as entering obediently and reluctance as entering only by the sword.
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r7.anchor: عن ابن زيد - رضي الله عنه - في الآية قال: من دخل طائعا هذا طوعا

DURR-FULL:v4p629/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r8.speaker: ربيع بن خثيم
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r8.claim: When prostrating at the thunder sūra’s prostration, Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym prayed to prostrate willingly to God.
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r8.anchor: إذا سجد في سجدة الرعد قال: بل طوعا يا ربنا

DURR-FULL:v4p629/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the shadows prostrate as each person’s shadow shifts right or left.
DURR-FULL:v4p629/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - في قوله {وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال} يعني حين يفيء ظل أحدهم عن يمينه أو شماله

DURR-FULL:v4p630/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p630/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v4p630/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says all shadows prostrate to God, citing the verse about shadows bowing humbly.
DURR-FULL:v4p630/r1.anchor: عن ابن زيد - رضي الله عنه - في قوله {وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال} قال: ذكر لنا أن ظلال الأشياء كلها تسجد لله

DURR-FULL:v4p630/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p630/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p630/r2.claim: Mujahid says the unbeliever’s shadow prays while he himself does not.
DURR-FULL:v4p630/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد - رضي الله عنه - في قوله {وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال} قال: ظل الكافر يصلي وهو لا يصلي

DURR-FULL:v4p630/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p630/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v4p630/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak describes shadows facing west at sunrise and east after noon until sunset.
DURR-FULL:v4p630/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك - رضي الله عنه - في الآية قال: إذا طلعت الشمس يسجد ظل كل شيء نحو المغرب فإذا زالت الشمس

DURR-FULL:v4p630/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p630/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p630/r4.claim: Al-Hasan takes the shadow to mean an unbeliever’s whole body and limbs, all obedient to God except the heart.
DURR-FULL:v4p630/r4.anchor: عن الحسن - رضي الله عنه - أنه سئل عن قوله {وظلالهم} قال: ألا ترى إلى الكافر فإن ظلاله جسده كله أعضاؤه لله مطيعة غير قلبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r1.claim: The clause continues 13:14: God alone has the true invocation, and prostration—the sign of divinity—is due to Him alone. Celestial beings and believers prostrate; polytheists do not prostrate to idols or ordinarily to God, though they may do so at times.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r1.anchor: وذلك شعار الإلهية ، فأما الدعوة فقد اختص بالحقة منها دون الباطلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r2.claim: The divine proper name replaces a pronoun, following the style used when the surah opens its main themes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r2.anchor: وعدل عن ضمير الجلالة إلى اسمه تعالى العلم تبعا للأسلوب السابق في افتتاح الأغراض الأصلية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r3.claim: The generic relative من conveys a conventional generality here: the great multitude, rather than an absolute enumeration.
