IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r3.anchor: والعموم المستفاد من من } الموصولة عموم عرفي يراد به الكثرة الكاثرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r4.claim: The two terms divide worshippers’ states: voluntary prostration comes from devotion, seeking closeness, glorification, and love; reluctant prostration comes from need or distress, as in 16:53.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r4.anchor: والمقصود من { طوعا وكرها } تقسيم أحوال الساجدين . والمراد بالطوع الانسياق من النفس تقربا وزلفى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r5.speaker: بعضهم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r5.claim: Some commentators take كرهًا as coercion or compulsion; Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects this as remote from the verse’s purpose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r5.anchor: وليس المراد من الكره الضغط والإلجاء كما فسر به بعضهم فهو بعيد عن الغرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r6.claim: Shadows are the forms of bodies produced when light is reflected onto them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r6.anchor: والظلال : جمع ظل ، وهو صورة الجسم المنعكس إليه نور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r7.claim: Their refers back to those in the heavens and earth, restricted by reason and ordinary experience to dense bodies that cast shadows; the phrase coordinates their shadows as another subject of prostration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r7.anchor: والضمير راجع إلى من في السماوات والأرض } مخصوص بالصالح له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r8.claim: Al-ghudu is the time when people leave for their needs; it may be a verbal noun with an omitted “time of,” or a plural of ghudwa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r8.anchor: والغدو : الزمان الذي يغدو فيه الناس ، أي يخرجون إلى حوائجهم : إما مصدرا على تقدير مضاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r9.claim: Āṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, the time when the sun yellows late in the day; naming dawn-going and evenings covers the full span of shadow times.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r9.anchor: والآصال : جمع أصيل ، وهو وقت اصفرار الشمس في آخر المساء ، والمقصود من ذكرهما استيعاب أجزاء أزمنة الظل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r10.claim: Shadows lie on the ground because bodies intercept sunlight, appearing like prostrators; their divinely created form symbolically testifies to God’s right to prostration even when people refuse or neglect it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r10.anchor: ومعنى سجود الظلال أن الله خلقها من أعراض الأجسام الأرضية ، فهي مرتبطة بنظام انعكاس أشعة الشمس عليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r11.claim: If two equal suns faced one another there would be no shadows; if the earth were transparent or glossy like water, shadows would not appear clearly. Their precise design signifies God’s uniqueness and creatures’ dependence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r11.anchor: ولو جعل الله الشمس شمسين متقابلتين على السواء لانعدمت الظلال ، ولو جعل وجه الأرض شفافا أو لامعا كالماء لم يظهر الظل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r12.claim: Earthly systems are arranged to serve several combined purposes, including signs of divine uniqueness and creaturely need; these signs are especially concentrated in humans, whose kind is uniquely ungrateful among animals.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p110/r12.anchor: وجعل نظام الموجودات الأرضية مهيئة لها في الخلقة لحكم مجتمعة ، منها : أن تكون رموزا دالة على انفراده تعالى بالإلهية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r11.claim: The statement may call attention to God’s power and the subjection of all things, or rebuke Quraysh: all in heaven and earth prostrate though they do not; al-Tabari favors the latter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305/r11.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون في ذلك طعن على كفار قريش وحاضري محمد عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r1.claim: Angels are included and prostrate willingly; earthly believers do likewise, while unbelievers prostrate reluctantly in one of two senses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r1.anchor: ومن تقع على الملائكة عموما، وسجودهم طوع بلا خلاف، وأما أهل الأرض فالمؤمنون منهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r2.claim: If prostration means the familiar physical act, Qatada takes reluctant unbelievers to be those compelled by the sword to accept Islam, hypocritically or under continuing initial compulsion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r2.anchor: فالمراد من الكفرة من يضمه السيف إلى الإسلام- كما قال قتادة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r3.claim: If prostration means submission and abasement, all unbelievers are included because afflictions humble them under God’s power; a poem uses ‘prostrate’ for hills bowed before hooves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r3.anchor: وإن جعلنا السجود الخضوع والتذلل- على حسب ما هو في اللغة كقول الشاعر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r4.speaker: النحاس والزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r4.claim: Al-Nahhas and al-Zajjaj say reluctant prostration refers to sinful believers and the lax; Ibn Atiyya finds this strained relative to the verse’s intended meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r4.anchor: وقال النحاس والزجاج: إن الكره يكون في سجود عصاة المؤمنين وأهل الكسل منهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r5.claim: The verse reports that shadows prostrate to God in the early mornings and evenings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r5.anchor: إخبار عن أن الظلال لها سجود لله تعالى بالبكر والعشيات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r6.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r6.claim: Al-Tabari connects this to 16:48, where shadows shift right and left in prostration; he says this is the afternoon shade.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r6.anchor: قال الطبري: وهذا كقوله تعالى: أولم يروا إلى ما خلق الله من شيء يتفيؤا ظلاله عن اليمين والشمائل سجدا لله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r7.claim: Mujahid says a disbeliever’s shadow prostrates willingly although its owner is reluctant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ظل الكافر يسجد طوعا وهو كاره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says an unbeliever’s shadow prostrates as it shifts from his right side to his left.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يسجد ظل الكافر حين يفيء عن يمينه وشماله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r9.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r9.claim: Some take ‘shadows’ to mean bodies or persons; Abu Ishaq (al-Zajjaj) weakens this interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r9.anchor: وحكى الزجاج أن بعض الناس قال: «الظلال» هنا يراد به الأشخاص- وضعفه أبو إسحاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r10.claim: Al-aṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, the late afternoon.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r11.speaker: أبو مجلز
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r11.claim: Abu Mujliz reads ‘wa al-īṣāl’; Abu al-Fath analyzes it as the verbal noun of ‘we entered evening,’ like becoming morning or evening.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز: «والإيصال» قال أبو الفتح: هو مصدر أصلنا أي دخلنا في الأصيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r12.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r12.claim: It is also reported that when an unbeliever prostrates to his idol, his shadow prostrates to God at that moment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p305#2/r12.anchor: وروي أن الكافر إذا سجد لصنمه فإن ظله يسجد لله تعالى حينئذ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p446/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p446/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p446/r1.claim: The verse declares God’s greatness and dominion: everything is subdued to Him, with believers prostrating willingly and polytheists unwillingly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p446/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن عظمته وسلطانه الذي قهر كل شيء، ودان له كل شيء.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p446/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p446/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p446/r2.claim: Al-ghuduww means early morning; al-asal is the plural of asil, the end of the day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p446/r2.anchor: وهو جمع أصيل وهو آخر النهار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p446/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p446/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p446/r3.claim: The prostration of shadows is linked to the verse describing created things’ shadows falling to the right and left in prostration to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p446/r3.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {أولم يروا إلى ما خلق الله من شيء يتفيأ ظلاله عن اليمين والشمائل سجدا لله

JISHUMI:v5p3766/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r5.claim: Sujud means submission or humility, and its root conveys making something low.

JISHUMI:v5p3766/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r6.speaker: الشاعر
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r6.claim: The cited poetic phrase describes hills bowing under the hooves.
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r6.anchor: ومنه: ترى الأكم فيها سجدا للحوافر

JISHUMI:v5p3766/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r7.claim: Zilal is the plural of zill, shadow.

JISHUMI:v5p3766/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r8.claim: Fay is shade that returns after the light has gone; zulla is related to covering or sheltering, and zill has the plural form zilal.
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r8.anchor: والفيء: الذي يرجع بعد ذهاب ضوئه، ومنه: الظلة، لسترها، وظل وظلال كرق ورقاق

JISHUMI:v5p3766/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r9.claim: Asil means late afternoon; asil has the plural asal, and asāl is a plural of that plural, associated with the evening's beginning.
JISHUMI:v5p3766/r9.anchor: والآصال: واحدها أصيل، وجمعها: أصل، وآصال جمع الجمع، وهو العشي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r1.claim: Qatāda says believers prostrate willingly and disbelievers unwillingly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r1.anchor: طوعا سجود المؤمن , وكرها سجود الكافر , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says some entered Islam willingly and others under threat of the sword.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r2.anchor: من دخل في الإسلام رغبة , { وكرها } من دخل فيه رهبة بالسيف , قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says long-standing Muslims have become accustomed to prostration, while new converts at first do it reluctantly until accustomed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r3.anchor: من طالت مدة إسلامه فألف السجود , { وكرها } من بدأ بالإسلام حتى يألف السجود , حكاه ابن الأنباري

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r4.speaker: بعض أصحاب الخواطر
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r4.claim: Some people of spiritual insight say a person becomes humble in adversity but grows weary when blessings continue.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r4.anchor: بعض أصحاب الخواطر أنه إذا نزلت به المصائب ذل

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r5.claim: Each person’s shadow prostrates with him: the believer’s shadow willingly and the disbeliever’s unwillingly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r5.anchor: ظل كل إنسان يسجد معه بسجوده , فظل المؤمن يسجد طائعا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r6.claim: Al-āṣāl is a plural of aṣl, itself a plural of aṣīl; aṣīl is late afternoon from ʿAṣr until sunset.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r6.anchor: والآصال جمع أصل , والأصل جمع أصيل , والأصيل العشي وهو ما بين العصر والمغرب

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r7.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb’s verse uses aṣāʾil for the late afternoons when one sits in the household’s courtyards.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p104#2/r7.anchor: لعمري لأنت البيت أكرم أهله … وأقعد في أفيائه بالأصائل

MUQATIL:13:15-16/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:13:15-16/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:13:15-16/r1.claim: Those in the heavens who prostrate to God are the angels; those on earth who do so willingly are the believers.
MUQATIL:13:15-16/r1.anchor: يعني الملائكة، { والأرض طوعا } ، يعني المؤمنين

MUQATIL:13:15-16/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:13:15-16/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:13:15-16/r2.claim: Even if disbelievers hate it, their shadows prostrate to God at sunrise and in the afternoon when the sun passes its zenith.
MUQATIL:13:15-16/r2.anchor: ظل الكافر كرها يسجد لله، وهو

NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r1.claim: Their prostration is worship and submission.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r2.claim: Willing prostration means angels and believers; unwilling means hypocrites and unbelievers under hardship.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ طوعا ﴾ حال يعنى الملائكة والمؤمنين ﴿ وكرها ﴾ يعنى المنافقين والكافرين في حال الشدة والضيق

NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r3.claim: “Their shadows” is coordinated with “whoever” and is plural of ẓill.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r4.claim: Ghudū is a plural like qanāh's plural qun; āṣāl is plural of aṣīl.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r4.anchor: ﴿ بالغدو ﴾ جمع غداة كقن وقناة ﴿ والآصال ﴾ جمع أصل جمع أصيل

NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r5.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r5.claim: Another view says every object's shadow prostrates morning and evening, the unbeliever's unwillingly and the believer's willingly.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p213#2/r5.anchor: قيل ظل كل شيء يسجد لله بالغدو والآصال وظل الكافر يسجد كرها وهو كاره وظل المؤمن يسجد طوعا وهو طائع

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and others say believers prostrate willingly while unbelievers do so under compulsion of the sword.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r1.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما: المؤمن يسجد طوعا، والكافر يسجد كرها بالسيف

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r2.claim: Qatāda also says an unbeliever submits unwillingly when faith can no longer benefit him.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r2.anchor: وعن قتادة أيضا: يسجد الكافر كارها حين لا ينفعه الإيمان

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r3.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets forced prostration as the subjection and mark of craftsmanship inherent in being created.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج: سجود الكافر كرها ما فيه من الخضوع وأثر الصنعة

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says voluntary means entering Islam out of desire and forced means entering from fear of the sword.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r4.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: { طوعا } من دخل في الإسلام رغبة، و { كرها } من دخل فيه رهبة بالسيف

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r5.claim: One view concerns believers only: long-established Muslims find prostration familiar, while others make themselves submit despite the hardship of religious duties until they grow accustomed to truth.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r5.anchor: وقيل: { طوعا } من طالت مدة إسلامه فألف السجود، و { كرها } من يكره نفسه لله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r6.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ's restrictive approach takes the general wording to mean believers and some who prostrate under coercion, such as hypocrites.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r6.anchor: فالآية محمولة على هؤلاء، ذكره الفراء

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r7.claim: A further believer-only view says some prostrate without difficulty while others bear the hardship of religious duty through faith until habituated to the truth.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r7.anchor: وقيل على هذا القول: الآية في المؤمنين منهم من يسجد طوعا لا يثقل عليه السجود

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r8.claim: Al-Qushayrī says the second approach is correct and keeps the verse general; one application is believers prostrate willingly while unbelievers are commanded and liable to prostrate.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r8.anchor: والمسلك الثاني: وهو الصحيح إجراء الآية على التعميم وعلى هذا طريقان

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r9.claim: The truest universal reading is that every creature, believing or unbelieving, prostrates as a created being, showing its need for its Maker, as all things glorify God in 17:44.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r9.anchor: والثاني: وهو الحق أن المؤمن يسجد ببدنه طوعا، وكل مخلوق من المؤمن والكافر يسجد

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r10.claim: Shadows prostrate because they appear and shift from side to side in morning and evening at God's direction, as in 16:48; Ibn ʿAbbās and others say this.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r10.anchor: أي ظلال الخلق ساجدة لله تعالى بالغدو والآصال لأنها تبين في هذين الوقتين

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r11.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r11.claim: Mujāhid says a believer's shadow prostrates willingly and an unbeliever's shadow unwillingly.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ظل المؤمن يسجد طوعا وهو طائع وظل الكافر يسجد كرها وهو كاره

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r12.speaker: ابن الأنباري
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r12.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says shadows have minds with which to prostrate, just as mountains were given understanding to speak.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r12.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: يجعل للظلال عقول تسجد بها، كما جعل للجبال أفهام

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r13.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r13.claim: Al-Qushayrī objects that a mountain might be given life and intellect, but a shadow is an accident and cannot be conceived as living.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r13.anchor: قال القشيري: في هذا نظر لأن الجبل عين، فيمكن أن يكون له عقل

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r14.claim: Prostration can mean inclination; Arabs say a palm tree prostrates when it leans.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r14.anchor: والسجود بمعنى الميل فسجود الظلال ميلها من جانب إلى جانب

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r15.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r15.claim: Al-Qushayrī explains shadow-prostration as its leaning from one side to another because shadows are effects and accidents.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r15.anchor: وأما الظلال فآثار وأعراض، ولا يتصور تقدير حياة لها

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r16.claim: Āṣāl is a plural of aṣl, itself a plural of aṣīl, the time from afternoon prayer until sunset; aṣāʾil is a further plural.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15/r16.anchor: و { الآصال } جمع أصل، والأصل جمع أصيل وهو ما بين العصر إلى الغروب

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15#2/r1.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb's poem uses aṣāʾil for late-afternoon periods, witnessing the word's plural form.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15#2/r1.anchor: لعمري لأنت البيت أكرم أهله وأقعد في أفيائه بالأصائل

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15#2/r2.claim: Wa-ẓilāluhum may coordinate with man or stand as a subject with an omitted predicate, meaning their shadows prostrate.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15#2/r2.anchor: والخبر محذوف التقدير: وظلالهم سجد بالغدو والآصال

QURTUBI-FULL:13:15#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15#2/r3.claim: Al-ghuduww may be a verbal noun or a plural of ghudwa; its plural sense is supported by its pairing with the plural āṣāl.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:15#2/r3.anchor: و { بالغدو } يجوز أن يكون مصدرا، ويجوز أن يكون جمع غداة

BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r1.claim: Prostrating literally means placing the forehead on the ground.
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r1.anchor: {ولله يسجد} حقيقة وهو بوضع الجبهة على الأرض.

BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r2.claim: Those in the heavens include angels, the spirits of prophets and saints, and believers of the higher ranks.
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r2.anchor: من في السموات يعني الملائكة وأرواح الأنبياء والأولياء وأهل الدرجات من المؤمنين

BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r3.claim: Those on earth include angels and believers among both humans and jinn.
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r3.anchor: والأرض من الملائكة والمؤمنين من الثقلين

BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r4.claim: Voluntary prostration is done by choice in both hardship and ease.
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r4.anchor: طوعا حال أي طائعين حالتي الشدة والرخاء

BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r5.claim: Reluctant prostration occurs under necessity or hardship, and applies to disbelievers, hypocrites, and devils.
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r5.anchor: وكرها أي : كارهين حالة الشدة والضرورة وذلك من الكافرين والمنافقين والشياطين

BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r6.claim: Another explanation distinguishes people born Muslim, who prostrate willingly, from captives taken from enemy territory, who do so unwillingly.
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r6.anchor: ويقال من ولد في الإسلام طوعا ومن سبى من دار الحرب كرها

BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r7.speaker: الحديث
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r7.claim: A hadith marvels at people led to Paradise in chains.
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r7.anchor: وفي الحديث : عجب ربك من قوم يساقون إلى الجنة بالسلاسل

BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r8.claim: Some devoted lovers refuse Paradise because they wish to remain in service; golden chains are placed around their necks to bring them in.
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r8.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن من أهل المحبة والوفاء من يطلب لدخول الجنة فيأبى ذلك طلبا للقيام بالخدمة فتوضع في أعناقهم السلاسل من الذهب

BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r9.speaker: كمال الخجندي
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r9.claim: Khujandi's verse says the garden of Paradise is not the lover's concern, illustrating devotion and aspiration beyond heavenly reward.
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r9.anchor:
قال الكمال الخجندي :
نيست ما راغم طوبى وتمناي بهشت
شيوه مردم نا اهل بودهمت ست

BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r10.claim: The phrase omits the verb سجود, supplying يسجد; shadows prostrate derivatively, following their owners.
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r10.anchor: وظلالهم على حذف الفعل ، أي : ويسجد ظلال أهل السموات والأرض بالعرض أي تبعا لذي الظل

BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r11.claim: Figuratively, prostration means submission to God's acts as He wills, while shadows submit through lengthening, shrinking, and shifting.
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالسجود معناه المجازي وهو انقيادهم لإحداث ما أراده الله فيهم شاؤوا أو كرهوا

BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r12.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r12.claim: Ghuduw is the morning, and āṣāl is the afternoon from the sun's zenith until sunset.
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r12.anchor: الغدو جمع غداة وهي البكرة والآصال جمع أصيل وهو العشي من حين زوال الشمس إلى غيبوبتها كما في بحر العلوم

BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r13.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r13.claim: Al-Kawashi and others define the aṣīl as the interval between afternoon prayer and sunset.
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r13.anchor: وقال في الكواشي وغيره : الأصيل ما بين العصر وغروب الشمس

BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r14.claim: The ب means في, making these times a ظرف for prostration; specifying them implies continuity, since submission is not confined to them.
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r14.anchor: والباء بمعنى في ظرف ليسجد أي يسجد في هذين الوقتين والمراد بهما الدوام

BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r15.claim: Morning and evening are singled out because shadows grow longer and more numerous then, although their movement and submission continue throughout the day.
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r15.anchor: وتخصيصهما مع أن انقياد الظلال وميلانها من جانب إلى جانب وطولها بسبب انحطاط الشمس وقصرها بسبب ارتفاعها لا يختص بوقت دون وقت

BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r16.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r16.claim: The inward reading identifies shadows with souls, which are shadows of spirits; the excerpt ends before completing its explanation of their prostration.
BURSEVI:v4p233#3/r16.anchor: قال في التأويلات النجمية وظلالهم أي نفوسهم فإن النفوس ظلال الأرواح وليس السجود بالطوع من شأن النفوس

RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r1.claim: One main interpretation takes prostration as placing the forehead on the ground; one subview limits the general wording to believers, some eager and others reluctant but self-compelling.
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r1.anchor: أن المراد منه السجود بمعنى وضع الجبهة على الأرض ، وعلى هذا الوجه ففيه وجهان : أحدهما : أن اللفظ وإن كان عاما إلا أن المراد به الخصوص وهم المؤمنون

RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r2.claim: The other subview keeps both wording and referent general, but raises the problem that unbelievers do not physically prostrate, unlike angels and believing jinn and humans.
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r2.anchor: والثاني : أن اللفظ عام والمراد منه أيضا العام وعلى هذا ففي الآية إشكال ، لأنه ليس كل من في السموات والأرض يسجد لله

RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r3.claim: One answer understands the general statement as a duty imposed on all, expressed as though it already occurred.
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r3.anchor: الأول : أن المراد من قوله : { ولله يسجد من فى * السماوات والارض }

RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r4.claim: Another answer makes prostration glorification and acknowledgment of servitude, which all creatures recognize; the verse cites 31:25.
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r4.anchor: أن المراد من السجود التعظيم والاعتراف بالعبودية ، وكل من في السموات ومن في الأرض يعترفون بعبودية الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r5.claim: A second main interpretation takes prostration as yielding and submission: God’s power and will operate throughout the heavens and earth.
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r5.anchor: السجود عبارة عن الانقياد والخضوع وعدم الامتناع وكل من في السموات والأرض ساجد لله بهذا المعنى

RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r6.claim: Al-Razi explains that everything besides the Necessary Existent is possible in itself and equally open to existence or nonexistence; neither is realized without an existing agent, so God creates all existence and nonexistence, and this universal dependence is prostration.
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r6.anchor: كل من كان كذلك امتنع رجحان وجوده على عدمه أو بالعكس ، إلا بتأثير موجود ومؤثر فيكون وجود كل ما سوى الحق سبحانه بإيجاده

RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r7.claim: Al-Razi compares this universal submission with 2:116, where everything in the heavens and earth is described as obedient to God.
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r7.anchor: ونظير هذه الآية : { بل له ما في * السماوات والارض * كل له قانتون }

RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r8.claim: He also links it to 3:83, which says those in the heavens and earth submit to God.
RAZI-FULL:v19p24#2/r8.anchor: وقوله : { وله أسلم من فى * السماوات والارض }
